task.description: Hard gate on ISS-0692's design amendment (SECURITY-REVIEWER originally raised this issue during REQ-362's own Step 2c gate on run WF02-REQ362-20260916). Verify the new §1.5 policy in lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md actually closes the PII-exposure gap, assess residual risk of relying on authoring-discipline alone, and run the standard INV-1..INV-8 scope test against the full diff since 35d3489a.
acceptance_criteria: Scope test run explicitly against the diff
Each of INV-1..INV-8 (and INV-9 if relevant) marked APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE with reasoning
Any APPLIES invariant independently verified, not taken on CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's word
Existing committed baseline PNGs independently visually inspected for PII, not just the sidecar text trusted

result.summary:
Checked out feature/WF03-ISS0692-20260917 at HEAD aaf60c24 (git fetch/pull --ff-only, up to date). Read ISS-0692.yaml, the full current lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md (not just §1.5 -- whole file for context), both step-02/step-02b handoffs (v1 FAIL and v2 PASS), and the full diff `git diff 35d3489a..HEAD -- lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts`.

SCOPE TEST: this is a design-doc amendment plus two comment-only annotations, not application code, a migration, a secret-resolving path, response-shaping code, or a lookup-by-ID handler in the literal sense. However it directly concerns a tenant-data-exposure-prevention policy for a permanently-git-committed artifact class (visual baselines) that this same role flagged during REQ-362's own gate -- treated as in-scope per the handoff's explicit framing and per this role's mandate to gate any change bearing on tenant-data exposure, not only literal code paths.

INVARIANT-BY-INVARIANT (per security-invariants.md):
- INV-1 (tenant data isolation / schema-per-tenant scoping): NOT-APPLICABLE in its literal mechanism sense -- no Ecto schema, migration, or query is touched by this diff. The *substance* INV-1 protects (tenant data must not leak outside its proper boundary) is what ISS-0692 raised in a different guise (permanent git artifact vs. cross-tenant DB read), and is addressed below under the general finding rather than forced into INV-1's checklist, which doesn't fit a documentation diff.
- INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response shaping, S4 not started.
- INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- S5 not started, unrelated to this diff.
- INV-4 (secrets by reference only): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no secret material, env var, or config resolution touched. Confirmed by reading the full diff; nothing resembling a credential appears in either changed file or in the three baseline PNGs/sidecar inspected.
- INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint, S4 not started.
- INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): NOT-APPLICABLE as a literal 'new data-access path' -- this diff adds no new path; it documents a content policy for an existing, already-gated mechanism (REQ-362, which itself already passed a SECURITY-REVIEWER gate that produced this very issue). This handoff itself is the artifact INV-6 asks for.
- INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no SQL anywhere in this diff.
- INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): NOT-APPLICABLE -- `web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts`'s diff is JSDoc-comment-only; verified independently below that no executable line changed, so there is no new error-handling surface to assess.
- INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request logic touched.

Since none of INV-1..9's literal checklists apply to a documentation diff, this gate's substantive work is the direct question the dispatch posed: does §1.5, if followed, actually close the gap this role originally raised, and is the residual risk acceptable.

DOES §1.5 CLOSE THE GAP: Yes, on the terms the original issue asked for. ISS-0692's FIX DIRECTION offered three options -- synthetic/seeded data requirement, a redaction step, or an explicit accepted-risk statement with reasoning. §1.5 selects the first, states it as 'a precondition of calling the accept action (§2.2) and the re-baseline action (§4.1), not a suggestion,' cross-references correctly from both call sites (verified directly: §2.2 and §4.1 each carry a 'Precondition (§1.5)' paragraph ahead of their numbered steps), and updates §7's AC map row. This matches the issue's own fix direction option 1 and additionally documents (not merely asserts) why the other two options were rejected, with reasoning I independently re-checked: the redaction-vs-§3.4-unconditional-diff argument is sound (§3.4's text, re-read directly, does say 'any pixel difference ... fails ... immediately and mechanically. No agent ... is consulted' -- a redaction mask genuinely cannot coexist with a zero-tolerance mechanical diff without becoming a new noise source), and the accepted-risk-not-worth-it argument is a reasonable value judgment given synthetic data costs nothing new (independently spot-checked: `test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/swiftroute/tenant-onboarding-happy.yaml` header does say 'Ported verbatim from R-Co ... disclosed-synthetic fixtures' and its actor is indeed fictional -- Alice Bauer / alice.bauer@swiftroute.example).

RESIDUAL GAP -- explicitly assessed: §1.5's own 'Enforcement note' is candid that this is authoring-discipline only, with zero mechanical enforcement -- 'is a judgment made by the scenario author and the accepting agent ... not a property derivable from image bytes. No code change is required.' This is a real residual gap (a future UAT-RUNNER or BA-persona run could still, in principle, accept a baseline against a real authenticated screen with real tenant data, and nothing in code stops it) but I assess it as an ACCEPTABLE residual risk for these independently-verified reasons, not merely because the design says so:
(a) The entire UAT scenario corpus this mechanism draws its actor/tenant data from is already synthetic-by-convention project-wide (re-confirmed above, consistent with `Letflow.Simulation.Runner`'s established discipline per the design's own citation) -- this isn't a new trust boundary being asked to hold, it's the same discipline every other tenant-data-adjacent fixture in this codebase already relies on.
(b) A mechanical PII-detection check (OCR/PII-scan on a screenshot before persist) does not exist anywhere in this codebase and would be a materially larger scope addition than ISS-0692 asked for or than this design-only WF-03 run is sized for -- appropriately deferred, not silently dropped, since §1.5 states the tradeoff reasoning in the design text itself rather than omitting it.
(c) The one path this mechanism has actually exercised end-to-end (REQ-362's own self-check, plus the ISS-0691 fail-case proof) was independently re-verified by me, not taken on trust: I opened all three committed PNGs directly (`01-EO-001.local.png`, and both `_disputed/ISS-0691/` evidence images) -- all three show the same unauthenticated Keycloak 'LETFLOW DEFAULT REALM' login form with empty username/password fields and a red 'REQ-362 deliberate visual-regression fail-case probe' banner; no actor name, email, company name, or any tenant-identifying content appears in any of the three images. This matches and extends CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's v2 re-gate finding (which inspected only the primary PNG) -- I additionally checked both `_disputed/` evidence images since they are also permanently git-committed artifacts under the same tree this policy governs, and found them equally clean.

VISUAL-BASELINE.TS DIFF: independently re-confirmed comment-only. `git diff 35d3489a..HEAD -- web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts` shows exactly two JSDoc block insertions (above `acceptBaseline` and `rebaseline`), each a `/** ... */` addition; no non-comment line is touched in either hunk. No functional change.

CONCLUSION: §1.5 satisfies ISS-0692's fix direction, is correctly cross-referenced and AC-mapped, contains no implementation code, and the accompanying comment-only annotations in visual-baseline.ts correctly signpost the same precondition at the call sites without attempting (and incorrectly claiming) mechanical enforcement. The residual reliance on discipline-not-mechanism is real but consistent with, and no weaker than, the trust model already governing every other synthetic-by-convention fixture in this codebase, and the one real committed artifact under this mechanism today was independently verified clean. No BLOCKER found on any applicable ground.
